days.Monday: Review unit fractions and counting beyond one whole; connect improper fractions and mixed numerals using concrete and visual models.
days.Tuesday: Locate and represent mixed numerals and improper fractions on number lines.
days.Thursday: Move flexibly between mixed numerals and improper fractions and explain the equivalence.
days.Friday: Consolidate representation, conversion and explanation through mixed problems and an exit assessment.

days.Monday: Analyse a model information report to identify its topic, purpose and intended audience.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how factual language and selected details match the report’s purpose and audience.
days.Thursday: Apply the focus by revising a short report section for a specified audience.
days.Friday: Edit a completed section to ensure its purpose and audience are clear.

days.Monday: Review equal intervals and locate unit fractions between zero and one.
days.Tuesday: Locate non-unit fractions and explain how the numerator and denominator determine position.
days.Thursday: Extend number lines beyond one whole and locate mixed numerals and improper fractions.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess locating, labelling and justifying fraction positions.

days.Monday: Analyse strong and weak classification openings.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to name the subject and place it in a broader category.
days.Thursday: Draft classification openings for students’ own report topics.
days.Friday: Edit and select the strongest opening for the report.

days.Monday: Compare fractions with the same denominator or numerator using visual models and precise language.
days.Tuesday: Compare fractions using benchmark values, especially one half and one whole.
days.Thursday: Compare fractions with unlike denominators using number lines or efficient equivalence.
days.Friday: Order fractions and justify an efficient comparison strategy independently.

days.Monday: Analyse how facts are grouped into logical sections.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to sort research notes and create clear subheadings.
days.Thursday: Organise students’ own notes into sections and draft the section order.
days.Friday: Review and improve the order and balance of the report sections.

days.Monday: Review prerequisite comparison strategies and identify when each strategy is useful.
days.Tuesday: Compare less obvious fractions using an efficient benchmark, number line or equivalent fraction.
days.Thursday: Solve and explain multi-step comparison and ordering problems using selected representations.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess independent strategy selection, ordering and mathematical justification.

days.Monday: Analyse effective topic sentences and identify what each paragraph will explain.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to write a topic sentence that introduces one clear paragraph focus.
days.Thursday: Draft topic sentences for the report’s planned sections.
days.Friday: Edit topic sentences for clarity, specificity and consistency.

days.Monday: Use area models and fraction strips to identify fractions that represent the same quantity.
days.Tuesday: Generate equivalent fractions by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same whole number.
days.Thursday: Find missing numerators or denominators and explain equivalence using models and symbols.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess recognition, generation and justification of equivalent fractions.

days.Monday: Analyse how a model paragraph develops a main idea with facts, examples and explanations.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to expand a simple factual sentence into a developed paragraph.
days.Thursday: Draft a complete paragraph using a topic sentence and supporting details.
days.Friday: Edit the paragraph to improve depth, relevance and factual precision.

days.Monday: Review generation of equivalent fractions and connect multiple representations.
days.Tuesday: Connect equivalent fractions across models, number lines and symbolic representations.
days.Thursday: Use equivalence to solve comparison, number-line and missing-value problems.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess flexible use of equivalence in unfamiliar contexts.

days.Monday: Identify technical words in a model and discuss how they support precision.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to select, explain and use subject-specific vocabulary.
days.Thursday: Revise a draft using more precise technical language and add glossary entries where needed.
days.Friday: Check that technical vocabulary is accurate, clear and not overused.

days.Monday: Connect tenths and hundredths fractions to place-value representations and decimal notation.
days.Tuesday: Convert fractions with denominators of 10 or 100 to decimal notation using place value.
days.Thursday: Use equivalent fractions to convert selected fractions to tenths or hundredths before writing decimals.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess fraction–decimal connections using representations and explanations.

days.Monday: Analyse how repeated key nouns, pronouns and linking phrases connect ideas.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to link sentences without making the paragraph repetitive.
days.Thursday: Revise a draft paragraph to improve flow and cohesion.
days.Friday: Edit the full section for clear connections within and between paragraphs.

days.Monday: Review tenths and hundredths and compare fraction and decimal representations of the same quantity.
days.Tuesday: Convert selected familiar fractions to decimals by first finding an equivalent fraction in tenths or hundredths.
days.Thursday: Locate and order related fractions and decimals on number lines.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess conversion, comparison and explanation across representations.

days.Monday: Compare objective information-report language with persuasive or exaggerated language.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to remove opinions, exaggeration and unsupported claims.
days.Thursday: Rewrite a draft section in a factual and neutral tone.
days.Friday: Edit the report for consistent objective language.

mathematics.topic: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator

days.Monday: Model addition of fractions with the same denominator and explain why the denominator remains unchanged.
days.Tuesday: Add fractions with the same denominator and explain why the denominator does not change.
days.Thursday: Model subtraction and solve worded or multi-step problems involving like-denominator fractions.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess calculation, representation and explanation.

days.Monday: Analyse the difference between copied notes, paraphrased facts and original explanation.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach how to paraphrase research notes and record the source.
days.Thursday: Turn students’ notes into original report sentences while retaining source details.
days.Friday: Check the report for accurate paraphrasing and complete source records.

days.Monday: Connect percentages to hundredths, decimals and visual models.
days.Tuesday: Represent and find common percentages such as 10%, 25%, 50% and 75% in practical contexts.
days.Thursday: Solve practical percentage problems involving quantities, money or simple data displays.
days.Friday: Consolidate and assess percentage representation, calculation and explanation.

days.Monday: Use the toolkit checklist to diagnose strengths and weaknesses in a complete model.
days.Tuesday: Explicitly teach a systematic editing process for structure, cohesion, vocabulary and accuracy.
days.Thursday: Edit and improve the complete student report using the toolkit checklist.
days.Friday: Complete the final proofread and prepare the report for publication.
